Front: Most common final diagnosis category in nontraumatic ED chest pain?
Back: Gastrointestinal causes (~42% in Fig 15-1); fewer than 15% have ACS

Front: Four acute life-threatening causes to exclude first in chest pain (Table 15-2)?
Back: Unstable ischemic heart disease, aortic dissection, pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism

Front: Most urgent noncardiopulmonary cause of chest pain?
Back: Esophageal rupture

Front: Time target for the ECG in acute chest pain?
Back: Within 10 minutes of arrival

Front: Serial ECG interval early in suspected ACS?
Back: Every 30-60 minutes (consider right-sided leads if nondiagnostic)

Front: Sensitivity of the resting ECG for ischemia?
Back: Poor; as low as 20%

Front: hs-troponin timing in suspected ACS?
Back: At presentation and repeat at 1-3 h (conventional assay: 3-6 h)

Front: Definition of MI by troponin?
Back: Rise and/or fall with at least one value above the 99th percentile, caused by ischemia

Front: Stable elevated troponin without ischemia (e.g., ESRD)?
Back: Chronic myocardial injury, not MI

Front: Type 1 vs type 2 MI?
Back: Type 1: acute coronary atherothrombosis; Type 2: oxygen supply-demand mismatch

Front: Chest pain history features that most increase likelihood of AMI?
Back: Radiation to both arms or the right arm/shoulder; also exertion, diaphoresis, nausea, 'pressure'

Front: Chest pain features that decrease likelihood of AMI?
Back: Pleuritic, positional, sharp, reproducible with palpation, inframammary

Front: Does chest wall tenderness exclude myocardial ischemia?
Back: No

Front: Does relief with nitroglycerin confirm ischemia?
Back: No; esophageal spasm also responds. Relief taking more than 10 min suggests non-ischemic pain or severe MI

Front: ECG features distinguishing pericarditis from STEMI?
Back: Diffuse ST elevation not in a single coronary territory plus PR depression

Front: Pericarditis pain: radiation and positional relief?
Back: Radiates to the trapezius ridge; relieved by sitting up and leaning forward

Front: Classic presentation of acute aortic dissection?
Back: Sudden tearing pain radiating to the back between the scapulae; hypertension; AI murmur; pulse deficit

Front: Why is TTE a poor test for aortic dissection?
Back: Poorly sensitive; CT or TEE are more practical

Front: Chest x-ray signs of pulmonary embolism?
Back: Hampton's hump and Westermark's sign

Front: Most common ECG finding in PE?
Back: Sinus tachycardia (also S1Q3T3 / right axis shift)

Front: HEART score low-risk threshold (without troponin)?
Back: 0-3, combined with troponin below the limit of quantification

Front: Low-risk chest pain with negative serial hs-troponin: further testing?
Back: None needed; discharge (stress testing hasn't been shown to improve outcomes)

Front: Intermediate-risk chest pain, no known CAD: preferred test?
Back: Coronary CT angiography

Front: Intermediate-risk chest pain with known obstructive CAD: preferred test?
Back: Stress nuclear or stress echo imaging (exercise if able)

Front: Are TIMI and GRACE scores used to diagnose ACS?
Back: No; they're prognostic scores for established ACS

Front: Outpatient with chest pain concerning enough to check troponin?
Back: Refer to the emergency department

Front: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy presentation?
Back: Abrupt chest pain after emotional or physical stress, ST elevation, raised troponin, no obstructive CAD
